pages.title: How to play PokéSurvivor
pages.description: Start your first PokéSurvivor run: controls, move switching, upgrade cards, healing and saving your progress.
pages.intro: Move your partner, collect experience and choose upgrades. Attacks fire automatically; positioning and the move you keep active are your main decisions.

sections.heading: Start a first run
steps: Open the developer’s browser game. Sign in for cloud progress or choose the guest option to try it locally.
Complete the personality questions, then accept the suggested partner or choose another starter. The quiz is a recommendation, not a permanent restriction on your choice.
Enter a run and move into open space. Your active move attacks automatically. Collect dropped experience while keeping an escape route.
When you level up, choose a new move, improve an existing move, or take a run stat upgrade. Read the effect before filling all your slots.

rows: Move
WASD or arrow keys
Drag on the play area
Choose active move
Tap a move at the bottom
Cycle moves
Q / E
Tap the move you need
Pause

sections.heading: Choose upgrades with a destination
paragraphs: A wider move collection is not automatically a stronger run: normally one selected move fires at a time. Improve an attack you can use reliably, then take a complementary move for a different range or matchup.

A move evolution needs its maximum level and a specific stat card taken in the same run. The golden evolution card is a separate choice. Use the evolution table before spending several levels on a plan.
Buff moves do not deal direct damage. Keep an actual damaging option available rather than making every slot a buff.

sections.heading: Recover and keep your progress
paragraphs: Use healing springs and read the terrain. Water slows movement and lava hurts; walls and trees can obstruct enemy projectiles. A chest with a lock needs you to remain beside it briefly.

Guest progress lives in this game origin’s browser storage. Clearing site data can remove it. A cloud account is the route for continuing on another device; this Wiki does not store or recover game saves.
A failed run is a useful checkpoint: compare whether you ran out of space, healing, or damage, and change that part of the next attempt.

sections.heading: Starting Move, active move and language
paragraphs: Buying Starting Move lets you choose a legal non-buff opening for that partner; it is separate from Repertoire, which adds a second opening move. During a run, learning a move no longer changes the active slot automatically. Use 1–4 or Q/E on desktop, or tap the move on touch devices, when you want to switch.

To change the game language, open Settings → Graphics → Language. The October 19 changelog lists French, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese in addition to the existing game languages. The game language and this Wiki’s language menu are separate settings.

sections.heading: Use the official game window
paragraphs: The current game source prevents play inside an iframe on another website and directs the player to pokesurvivor.com. Open the official site directly instead of using a proxy, copied login form or paid workaround. This Wiki provides guides and does not embed or operate the game.

pages.title: PokéSurvivor on Android & iPhone: Controls & Fixes
pages.description: Play PokéSurvivor on Android, iPhone or iPad with touch or a supported controller; install the PWA, protect saves and diagnose current mobile reports.
pages.intro: PokéSurvivor runs in a mobile browser on Android, iPhone and iPad. Use the touch controls, or a supported controller where available, and customize the touch layout in Settings → Controls. Manual Aim is not available on mobile in the reviewed October 20 source.

sections.heading: Set up touch controls
steps: Open pokesurvivor.com in Android Chrome or iPhone/iPad Safari and rotate the device to landscape.
Choose a guest session or your game account. Start a run and drag on the play area to move; the joystick appears at the touch position.
Open Settings → Controls → Place the buttons. Drag attack buttons, pause and the joystick into reachable positions; choose a fixed or floating joystick.
Try a short run before relying on a long session. Screen size, browser support and device performance can differ.

sections.heading: Controller and touch targeting
paragraphs: The October 18 build added broad controller support. The reviewed October 20 source then removed Manual Aim on mobile. Desktop or controller behavior and touch behavior must therefore be diagnosed separately.

On a phone or tablet, use the touch joystick and tap the move slot you want. Do not look for Settings → Accessibility → Manual Aim on mobile. A controller connected to a browser device does not make this a native console release.

sections.heading: Device-specific checkpoints
paragraphs: Android Chrome usually exposes Install app or Add to Home screen in its browser menu. iPhone and iPad use Safari’s Share → Add to Home Screen. A home-screen icon is still the official web app, not a native store package.

On iPad, test landscape, full-screen behavior and the joystick before a long run. Browser UI and multitasking can reduce the usable play area. This guide does not label a simulator result as a physical-device test.

sections.heading: Controller detected but movement does not respond
paragraphs: Issue #206 reports a detected controller whose movement failed. Issue #259 separately reports a touch joystick that stayed locked after a level-up or notification. These are player reports, not reproduced universal defects.

Record the device category, browser, controller model if any, and whether the failure started after a card or notification. Save first if possible before reloading or restarting. Do not clear site data as a routine test.

sections.heading: Add the game to your home screen
paragraphs: On Android, look in your browser’s menu for an install or Add to Home screen option. On iPhone or iPad, look in Safari’s Share menu for Add to Home Screen. Wording and availability vary by browser and OS.

This adds the browser app, not a separate native App Store release. The project includes an offline cache, but a fresh install still needs resources to load, and online account or co-op functions need a connection. This guide has not certified offline behavior on every device.

sections.heading: If the run feels slow
steps: Pause and lower the graphics quality in Settings, or try automatic quality.
Reduce damage-number effects and screen shake if they distract you or add load.
Close other demanding tabs, then test another short run. Do not clear the game’s site data as a routine performance fix.

sections.heading: If your collection looks missing
paragraphs: Check that you opened the same game address, browser profile and account as before. A different domain or private-browsing session has separate browser storage.
If you used a cloud account, sign back into that account. If you played as a guest and erased its storage, installing a home-screen shortcut does not reconstruct the missing save.

sections.heading: Change controls and language safely
paragraphs: Use Settings → Controls for touch-button placement and controller mapping, and Settings → Graphics → Language for the game language. Manual Aim was removed on mobile in the reviewed October 20 source.

Issue #258 reports missing move or map graphics after a tab switch or screen lock. Save first if possible, then reload the current page. Record whether the problem returns; no cause is confirmed and clearing storage is not a safe diagnostic step.

pages.description: Plan a legal PokéSurvivor starter build, verify its opening move and evolution requirement, and create a shareable route.
pages.intro: Choose a starter, verify the opening move’s physical or special category, and pair it with a compatible route. The planner preserves existing p and m share links and never reads your account.

sections.heading: Match the move to the correct offensive stat
paragraphs: Physical moves scale from Attack and special moves from Special Attack. Swords Dance and Dragon Dance boost only physical Attack; Nasty Plot is a shared Normal-pool buff that boosts Special Attack and can be selected for a special route such as Charmander with Ember.

A move evolution can still require the Power card recorded by the current source even when the move is special. That eligibility card and the damage-scaling stat are separate rules; this guide does not invent a replacement evolution requirement.

sections.heading: A repeatable upgrade order
steps: Check your starter’s actual starting move in the starter table. Two partners of the same type can start with different moves.
When offered, take the stat card required by that move’s evolution. The condition is taking it in the current run, not buying an unrelated permanent improvement.
Raise the move to its maximum level. Choose the golden evolution card when it is offered.
Add another damaging move from your partner’s type pool or the shared Normal pool. Select it when the matchup or attack pattern makes it more useful.

sections.heading: Tradeoffs that change your decisions
paragraphs: An attack’s raw damage does not account for missed shots, travel, area coverage or enemy resistance. Do not compare a persistent aura and a projectile as if damage divided by cooldown measured identical things.

Melee moves require closer positioning. The snapshot includes a melee balance change in the move definitions, so older tables may disagree with this reference. Inspect both the current move and the risk of staying in range.
Stat upgrades, terrain and weather can change a run. Treat the routes above as starting plans and use the type calculator when your damage seems unexpectedly low.

pages.title: PokéSurvivor Download? Play Online, PWA & APK Explained
pages.description: Play the official PokéSurvivor browser game, install its PWA and understand third-party APK ports, saves and account limitations.
pages.intro: Play the official PokéSurvivor in a current browser at pokesurvivor.com. On phones and supported desktop browsers, installing the PWA adds that same site to your home screen. There is no verified official APK or native app-store package in this source snapshot.

sections.heading: Open the official version first
steps: Open pokesurvivor.com in a current Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox browser.
Play in the browser. If your browser offers Install app or Add to Home Screen, use that menu to install the PWA.
Sign in or link the account before changing browser profiles, clearing site data or moving devices.
Treat any APK, native installer or similarly named game as a separate third-party product until its publisher and version are verified.

sections.heading: Saves, accounts and required updates
paragraphs: The current source saves normal progress immediately in this browser. Cloud upload now happens when you press the Save button, plus the game’s before-update and before-logout paths. The older 10-minute and 30-minute automatic schedules are historical behavior and must not be used as current guidance.

Save can show local, pending, syncing, success or offline. Pending and the 65-second wait between successful uploads do not mean the cloud write completed. Before moving devices, press Save and wait for the visible success state on the first device.
The official cloud features work on pokesurvivor.com. A guest copy is not guaranteed to be recoverable or portable, and this Wiki cannot merge competing device copies.

sections.heading: Before opening a download
paragraphs: Check the exact game name, publisher and platform. This Wiki does not mirror installers or claim that an unverified helper APK is an official release.
A search for Pokémon Survivor Burst can lead to a different downloadable game by ClessioTV. Its files and instructions do not install the browser game documented here.
For the original source project, use the upstream repository linked in our source notes. Keep a local copy separate from the live game and do not assume a browser save transfers between addresses.

sections.heading: Does an iOS or Android listing exist?
paragraphs: This source snapshot documents browser/mobile and PWA support. It is not evidence of a native App Store or Google Play listing. Use the mobile guide for the supported browser route instead of treating every search result with the name as the same product.

sections.heading: Official site and embedded copies
paragraphs: The current developer notice prevents the game from running inside a third-party iframe and provides a button to the official site. If an embedded window says the game is available only on its official website, open pokesurvivor.com directly. Do not use a proxy or copied account form.
This restriction does not create a new APK or native store build. Android and iPhone players still use the official browser version or add its PWA to the home screen.

pages.title: PokéSurvivor Co-op Not Working? Connecting & Reconnecting
pages.description: Check PokéSurvivor friends, room invites, Connecting and Reconnecting loops, cross-network reports and rift-boss symptoms without risking a save.
pages.intro: Find the exact co-op stage that failed: accepted friendship, three-minute room invitation, browser peer connection, or the running game. An accepted friend can be invited without an Online indicator in the current source.

sections.heading: Start with friends
steps: Sign into the game’s cloud account on the developer’s site.
Open Friends and add your friend by their nickname.
Invite them to your room, check that everyone has joined, then start the group run.
Keep an internet connection available. Offline browser play does not provide online multiplayer.

sections.heading: Could not connect: what to check first
paragraphs: “Could not connect” is a player-reported symptom in GitHub issue #164, not proof that every player is in a confirmed global outage. Check both players are on pokesurvivor.com, signed in, on the current build and using automatic date and time. Then reload both pages and create one new room.
If the new room still fails, record the time, browser, device, the host/guest role, failed stage and exact on-screen status. Do not publish a room code, email, password, token or save data.

sections.heading: Boss bar appears but the boss does not
paragraphs: GitHub issue #193 reports a co-op run where a boss health bar appeared without the boss, followed by later rifts no longer appearing. That report was filed on October 18; it is not the same as the October 14 changelog fix for invisible enemies after a rift.

Reload onto the current build and try a fresh room. If it repeats, report the host/non-host role, run time, rift sequence and whether ordinary enemies remained visible. This Wiki cannot claim a fix until the developer publishes one.

sections.heading: Password and account recovery
paragraphs: The October 14 changelog adds linking an existing username/password account to Gmail. If you linked it, using Sign in with Google with that Gmail is intended to open the same account.

The game’s login notice says an unlinked account cannot be recovered through that Google route. Do not type passwords into this Wiki or an unofficial recovery form; we cannot restore the developer’s accounts.

sections.heading: Reports after switching networks
paragraphs: Player reports #207 and #212 describe connection failures that continued after switching between Wi-Fi and mobile data. Changing networks is therefore one diagnostic step, not a guaranteed fix. Check both players’ current build, exact error, signed-in state and room role before trying a fresh room.
A connection failure alone does not show that either collection was deleted. Do not clear site data or enter credentials into an unofficial recovery form while diagnosing co-op.

sections.heading: Separate reports from confirmed fixes
paragraphs: GitHub issues #164, #192 and #193 are player reports and can describe different symptoms. Treat each as reported evidence until a developer changelog or source change confirms the cause and fix. The October 14 changelog does confirm specific invite, pause and invisible-enemy fixes, but it does not automatically close every later boss or rift report.
Checked on 2026-10-20. When reporting a repeat, include host/non-host role, browser, approximate run time and visible message; never publish room codes or account data.

sections.heading: Four stages: find where co-op stopped

rows: Friendship

That a room invitation was received

That the peer connection is ready
Peer connection
The game reports the browser-to-host link is established
That every later event will synchronize
Running game
The host starts and all players see the expected encounter
That a missing boss is the same problem as a connection loop

sections.heading: Connecting, relay and disconnect reports checked October 21
paragraphs: Issue #260 reports an initial connection failure. Issue #253 reports a disconnect after play had already started. Keep these stages separate and record host or guest, device category, visible room status and game version. Their timing near the pilot commit does not prove the pilot caused either report.

Commit 3c9641c integrates a client TURN pilot: the browser still prefers a direct connection, requests credentials from ice.pokesurvivor.com for authorized accounts, and falls back to STUN-only behavior when credentials are unavailable. A relayed room can display “Connected (via server)”. This is source evidence, not proof of universal availability or success.

sections.heading: Boss missing after a rift
paragraphs: This is an already-running-game symptom, not the initial connection stage. The updated October 19 changelog describes a boss spawning too far away after returning from a rift and a change that spawns it nearby or relocates it when too far away.
Check the visible game version and record whether the symptom still occurs. A published boss-spawn change is not evidence that room-connection failures are fixed.

sections.heading: Privacy-safe co-op evidence
paragraphs: Report only platform or device category, visible game version, host or guest role, the failed stage and the visible status. Do not publish IP addresses, room codes, tokens, TURN credentials or raw WebRTC dumps.
A direct connection is preferred; server relay is a fallback for authorized pilot accounts. “Connected (via server)” describes the selected path, not a different gameplay mode.

pages.title: PokéSurvivor Save Recovery: Safe Account Checklist
pages.description: Use a privacy-safe PokéSurvivor save and account recovery checklist for missing progress, Google linking, 409 errors and Paused to protect your progress.
pages.intro: Stop before clearing data, uninstalling a PWA or overwriting a working copy. This guide does not read, upload or repair a save. It helps you preserve evidence and choose the safest next step.

sections.heading: Safety rules before troubleshooting
paragraphs: Never paste a password, session token, room code, email address or save file into this Wiki. Do not edit a database, import unknown scripts or keep retrying writes against the only browser profile that still shows your progress.

If one browser, profile or device still shows the correct account, leave it open and unchanged. Record only non-sensitive facts such as browser name, device type, visible nickname, approximate time and the exact error text.

sections.heading: Save now and confirm the result
paragraphs: Normal progress is written to this browser first. In the reviewed October 21 source, cloud upload is manual: press Save. The game also attempts the same path before a required update and before logout. The old 10-minute and 30-minute schedules remain historical notes, not current promises.

Read the visible state literally: local means this browser has the copy; pending or waiting means upload is not confirmed; syncing means a request is in progress; success confirms the current upload; offline means the cloud request could not complete. Successful uploads are kept at least 65 seconds apart.

For a device handoff, finish on device A, press Save, wait for success, then open device B. Do not make progress on both devices and assume every field will merge. Closing the tab, forcing logout or clearing storage is not a safe substitute for a confirmed Save.

sections.heading: Paused to protect your progress and 409 reports
paragraphs: Issue #185 is a player report describing “Paused to protect your progress” together with a 409 response while setting a name. The report says private browsing and another browser did not solve it. This is evidence of one reported symptom, not a confirmed universal cause or a recovery guarantee.

Preserve any browser that still displays progress. Note the exact message, time, browser and whether the account was linked. Use the diagnostic below to create a non-sensitive report; submit it only through the developer’s official support or issue tracker.

sections.heading: What the October 14 Gmail change means
paragraphs: The official changelog says an existing username/password account can be linked to Gmail, and Sign in with Google with that Gmail should then open the same account. It also warns that an unlinked account cannot be recovered through that Google route.

Account linking is preventive. It does not prove that an unlinked guest save can be reconstructed after browser data is gone, and this independent Wiki has no access to the developer’s account database.

sections.heading: What this checklist cannot promise
paragraphs: An unlinked guest is not guaranteed to be recoverable. A cloud account helps portability, but this guide cannot guarantee mid-run continuity or reconstruct a copy whose browser storage is gone.
The current upload path no longer pre-reads an older cloud copy before writing. That reduces extra reads; it is not a promise that competing device copies will be merged.

pages.intro: PokéSurvivor and Pokémon Survivor Burst are different fan projects. A similar name does not make their rosters, download files or move systems interchangeable.

sections.heading: Why the distinction changes the answer
paragraphs: An APK tutorial for one project does not establish mobile support for the other. A move evolution condition in our table describes the browser project’s code; it is not a Burst build guide.

If your game has the Burst modes described above, use ClessioTV’s release thread and its linked community. If you are choosing a partner in the browser game, our starter and move references apply to the recorded source snapshot.

pages.title: About this Wiki & editorial method
pages.description: How Pokémon Survivor Wiki checks game mechanics, labels recommendations and separates source data from gameplay tests.
pages.intro: Pokémon Survivor Wiki is an independent English reference for jpter78’s PokéSurvivor. We do not develop the game and are not an official Pokémon website.

sections.heading: Where the information comes from
paragraphs: Database tables are generated from the local game repository. Every snapshot records its source commit and file checksums. The source notes below each guide point to the files used for that topic.
The snapshot review date means the files were reviewed for this build. It does not mean that the live game was retested that day, or that the Wiki synchronizes automatically with every new release.

sections.heading: How recommendations are labeled
paragraphs: Starter score bands are a transparent comparison of starting stats, not a measured survival-time leaderboard. Build routes combine documented starting moves, evolution prerequisites and practical editorial advice.

We do not describe source inspection as firsthand playtesting. Recommendations should be revisited after balance changes; a numerical score cannot account for player skill, terrain, co-op or an entire run’s upgrades.

sections.heading: Credits and rights
paragraphs: Game code through commit b297089 was released under MIT. Code published after October 14, 2026 uses PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. This Wiki uses source inspection for factual explanation and does not redistribute the later game code. Pokémon data in the original project was obtained from PokéAPI.

This Wiki build does not distribute the original SpriteCollab Pokémon sprites. Pixelify Sans is provided under the SIL Open Font License; the license accompanies the font files. We have no affiliation with the game developer or Pokémon rights holders.

This site has no game account system, paid downloads, token sales or cryptocurrency. For game bugs use the developer’s linked source repository. Source discrepancies can be checked against the file and snapshot references on the affected page.

pages.title: Privacy & local tools
pages.description: What the Wiki’s local search, filters and calculators do, and how external game services differ from this reference site.
pages.intro: Search, filters and calculators run in your browser. Optional Google Analytics measures page visits only after you choose Allow analytics. This Wiki has no game accounts or advertising scripts.

sections.heading: Search and calculators
paragraphs: The site downloads its static search index and reference data from the same host. A search query appears in the page URL, so a hosting provider may receive it as part of a normal request. Do not enter passwords or other private information in search.
The evolution checker reads your selected move, level and prerequisite. It does not connect to the game, inspect your collection or modify a save.

sections.heading: Hosting and external sites
paragraphs: Serving web pages can involve standard request logs such as IP address, requested path and browser information at the hosting provider. Exact retention depends on the configured provider; this page does not promise an unverified retention period.
The developer’s game, GitHub and other external destinations have their own data practices. The game’s cloud login and save services are separate from this Wiki.

sections.heading: Optional Google Analytics
paragraphs: Google Analytics 4 (measurement ID G-GEQDCG9L1K) measures page visits and basic technical information after you allow analytics. Google receives the page path, browser/device information and network information needed to deliver its service. Search query strings and URL fragments are removed from the configured page location and referrer. Automatic search, form, outbound-click, video and download measurement are disabled. We do not send game saves, account information or search terms as custom events.

Before your choice, the Wiki does not load the Google tag. Your choice is stored locally under psw-analytics-consent-v1. When allowed, Google Analytics can set first-party _ga cookies to distinguish visits. Use Analytics preferences in the footer to change your choice; declining stops analytics storage and clears accessible Analytics cookies. Browsers signaling Global Privacy Control do not start analytics.

Google Analytics is provided by Google. See https://policies.google.com/privacy and https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout for Google privacy information and its browser opt-out tool. The host may still process ordinary delivery logs independently of this optional choice.
